You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Fed’s Third-in-Command Signals Steady Policy Stance; SanDisk and Micron Lead AI Sector Gains Amid Divergent US Stocks; PCE Inflation Beats Expectations, Heightening Policy Uncertainty

TEXT:
I. Hot News
Fed Developments New York Fed President Williams: Current monetary policy stance is appropriate; inflation significantly above 2% is an undisputed fact.
Williams stated that tariffs, energy prices, and AI investment are the main drivers of current inflation. He expects inflation to fall to around 3.5% by the end of 2026 and return to the 2% target by 2028; unemployment will decline to 4%.
He emphasized that current interest rate levels are sufficient to help inflation return to target, but significant risks remain, and policy must stay flexible.
Market impact: This reinforces expectations of the Fed maintaining “higher rates for longer,” short-term pressure on rate-cut bets, a strong US dollar index, and some pressure on risk assets.
International Commodities Iran-related developments around the Strait of Hormuz continue to ferment, testing the US-Iran ceasefire agreement.
Iran is expected to generate approximately $40 billion annually from the Strait of Hormuz and has proposed joint toll collection with neighboring countries. Meanwhile, Iran’s Revolutionary Guard attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship near the strait, testing the implementation of the ceasefire.
Background: Previous Middle East conflicts drove up energy prices and thus US inflation. Ceasefire progress had previously pulled oil prices lower, but this incident highlights the fragility of the agreement.
Market impact: Oil prices faced short-term downward pressure, but geopolitical uncertainty continues to provide support for the energy market. Gold and other safe-haven assets were temporarily dragged down by the stronger dollar.
Macroeconomic Policy US May PCE Price Index rose 4.1% YoY, first time above 4% since April 2023.
Key drivers include energy price increases from the Middle East conflict and early effects of Trump’s tariff policies. Q1 GDP final reading was revised up to 2.1%, but downward revision to private domestic purchases indicates weak consumption momentum.
Institutions forecast US unemployment may rise to 4.7% by year-end, with hiring becoming more cautious.
Market impact: Stickier-than-expected inflation, combined with Fed officials’ comments, further narrowed market expectations for the number of rate cuts this year, supporting the dollar and US Treasury yields.
II. Market Review
Commodities Forex Performance
Spot Gold: $4,021/oz, -0.14%
Spot Silver: $57.40/oz, -0.72%
WTI Crude: $71.70/bbl, -0.33%
Brent Crude: $75.20/bbl, -0.4%
US Dollar Index (DXY): 101.51, -0.02%
Driver Analysis : The dollar index held firm near the strong 101.5 range, driven by Fed officials’ “higher rates for longer” signals and sticky US inflation data. Gold and silver came under pressure and corrected amid the strong dollar and fluctuating risk sentiment, though Middle East geopolitical uncertainty still provided some safe-haven support. Oil prices edged lower amid intertwined US-Iran ceasefire progress and Hormuz Strait events, as expectations of supply recovery rose, but the fragility of the agreement limited downside. In the short term, dollar movements and the Fed policy path remain the core variables for precious metals and energy prices. Institutions generally believe that if inflation data continues to beat expectations, precious metals may stay range-bound, while oil prices need to watch actual geopolitical developments and OPEC+ dynamics.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC: $59,595, -2%
ETH: $1,565, +3.25%
Total Crypto Market Cap: $2.14 trillion, -1.4%
24h Total Liquidations: ~$887 million (longs ~$691 million)
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map: Current BTC price ~$59,576. Large long liquidation clusters in the $58,500–$59,300 range below; breaking key support could trigger cascading long stops and accelerate downside. Significantly larger short liquidation pools above in the $60,000–$62,500 range. Overall liquidity still leans toward upward price attraction, but shorts may dominate in the near term if $59,000 is not held.
Spot ETF Net Flows: BTC spot ETFs saw net outflows of $414 million yesterday and $469 million the day before, totaling $997 million over three consecutive days.

Summary Driver Analysis : US stocks showed clear divergence. AI infrastructure-related memory and chip stocks surged (Micron, SanDisk, etc., up over 15%), reflecting optimism about the sustainability of AI capex. In contrast, consumer tech giants like Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon faced selling pressure due to product price hikes, with Apple’s single-day drop of over 6% marking its largest since April 2025. Drivers differed significantly: memory stocks benefited from strong AI data center demand for HBM and storage chips, with Micron’s earnings beating expectations directly boosting the sector. Big tech names, however, were forced to raise prices due to rapidly rising storage chip costs, raising market concerns about demand elasticity and margins. Overall sector trends show AI themes still fermenting, but high-valuation consumer tech faces cost-pass-through pressure. Institutions believe this divergence will persist, with capital favoring high-visibility AI supply-chain names.
[...]
NVDA: $233M
[...]
Driver Analysis : Micron’s quarterly results significantly beat expectations and raised full-year guidance, primarily due to explosive growth in demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) driven by AI training and inference. Current HBM3/HBM3E offers several times the capacity and bandwidth of the previous generation. NVIDIA’s next-gen Blackwell GPUs require 3-8 times more HBM than prior generations, keeping global HBM supply tight. As one of the few firms with HBM mass-production and design capabilities, Micron’s order visibility has risen sharply, ASPs are moving higher, directly driving margin expansion and earnings beats. Semiconductor equipment makers like Applied Materials benefit from capex on advanced packaging, 3D stacking, and memory line expansions. Storage players like Western Digital also rose on strong AI data center demand for high-speed NAND flash.
[...]
This rally contrasts sharply with consumer-end big tech (e.g., Apple and Microsoft raising prices due to surging storage costs, triggering sell-offs), highlighting differentiated pricing between “high-ROIC AI capex certainty” and “weaker consumer demand elasticity.” Even against the backdrop of May PCE rising to 4.1% and Fed’s Williams signaling “higher rates for longer,” AI-related supply chains are viewed as non-discretionary growth tracks. Capital continues flowing into pure AI-enabling segments. Institutions believe that if hyperscaler capex guidance remains strong (historical data shows high AI ROI visibility), excess returns in memory and equipment sectors may extend into 2027. However, risks include macro data deterioration or geopolitical escalation slowing overall tech spending. Short-term technicals show some profit-taking pressure; investors are advised to watch for phased buying on pullbacks and Q3 capacity ramp validation.
[...]
BlackBerry, once famous for physical-keyboard phones, has quietly become a key software provider for “physical AI” and robotics ecosystems. Its QNX software framework is called the “never-crash” autonomous machine nervous system, providing safe, reliable, deterministic real-time operating systems for smart cars and warehouse robots to chip makers like NVIDIA and AMD.
